until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do.

And they will say to their skins, ‘Why did you bear witness against us?’ They will say, ‘God made us speak, Who gave speech to all things. And He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned.
And you did not use to conceal yourselves, lest your hearing or your eyes or your skins should bear witness against you; but you thought that God did not know most of what you did.
And that supposition of yours which you supposed of your Lord has ruined you. So you have become among the losers’.
So if they endure the Fire will [still] be their abode; and if they seek reconciliation, then they will not be among the reconciled.

And We have assigned them companions, who have adorned for them that which is before them, and that which is behind them. And the word became due against them, being among communities that passed away before them of jinn and mankind. Truly they were losers.
And those who disbelieve say, ‘Do not listen to this Qur’ān and hoot it down that perhaps you might prevail’.
But verily We will make those who disbelieve taste a severe chastisement, and We will verily requite them the worst of what they used to do.
That is the requital of God’s enemies — the Fire! Therein will be their everlasting abode as a requital for their denial of Our signs.

And those who disbelieve will say: ‘Our Lord, show us those who led us astray from among the jinn and mankind so that we may have them underneath our feet [to trample them], that they may be among the lowermost’.

Truly those who say, ‘Our Lord is God!’ and then remain upright, the angels descend upon them, [saying to them], ‘Do not fear, nor grieve, and rejoice in the good tidings of the paradise which you were promised.
We are your friends in the life of this world, and in the Hereafter, and therein you will have whatever your souls desire, and therein you will have whatever you request,
as a hospitality from One Forgiving, Merciful’.
And who speaks better [words] than him who summons [others] to God, and acts righteously and says, ‘Indeed I am one of those who submit [to God]’?
And they are not equal, the good deed and the evil deed. Repel with that which is better then, behold, he between whom and you there was enmity will be as though he were a dear friend.
But none is granted it, except those who are steadfast; and none is granted it except one [deserving] of a great reward.
And if some temptation from Satan should provoke you, then seek refuge in God. Truly He is the Hearer, the Knower.
And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun and moon, but prostrate to God Who created them, if it is Him Whom you worship.
But if they disdain, still those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they tire not.

And among His signs is that you see the earth desolate, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Truly He Who revives it is indeed the Reviver of the dead. Surely He has power over all things.

Indeed those who blaspheme Our signs are not hidden from Us. Is one who is cast into the Fire better [off], or one who arrives secure on the Day of Resurrection? Act as you wish; indeed He is Seer of what you do.
Truly those who disbelieve in the Remembrance when it comes to them [are not hidden from us], and truly it is an unassailable Book:
falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it, [it is] a revelation from One Wise, Praised.
Nothing is said to you, except what has already been said to the messengers before you. Surely your Lord is One of forgiveness and [also] One of painful punishment.

And had We made it a non-Arabic Qur’ān, they would have said, ‘Why have its signs not been explained [clearly]? What! non-Arabic and an Arab?’ Say: ‘For those who believe it is guidance and a healing; but as for those who do not believe, there is a deafness in their ears, and they are blind to it. Those, they are [as if they were being] called from a distant place’.

And verily We gave Moses the Scripture, but differences arose concerning it; and were it not for a Word that had [already] preceded from your Lord, judgement would have been made between them; for indeed they are in grave doubt concerning it.
Whoever acts righteously, it is for [the good of] his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is to the detriment thereof. And your Lord is not [at all] a tyrant to His servants.

To Him devolves [all] knowledge of the Hour. And no fruit emerges from its sheath, and no female bears [child] or delivers except with His knowledge. And on the day when He will call out to them, ‘Where [then] are My associates?’ they will say, ‘We proclaim to You that there is no witness amongst us’.
And what they used to call on before has forsaken them and they suppose that there is no refuge for them.
Man never wearies of supplicating for good, but should any ill befall him, then he becomes despondent, despairing.

And if We let him taste mercy from Us after the harm that had befallen him, he will surely say, ‘This is my due! I do not think that the Hour will ever set in, and even if I am returned to my Lord, I will indeed have the best [reward] with Him’. But We will assuredly inform those who disbelieve of what they did, and assuredly We will make them taste a harsh chastisement.
And when We bestow graces upon man, he shows disregard and turns aside; but when ill befalls him, he makes prolonged supplications.
Say: ‘Consider [this]: if it is from God, and you disbelieve in it, who will be further astray than one who is in extreme defiance?’
We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own souls until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient that your Lord is witness to all things?
Nay, verily they are in doubt about the encounter with their Lord. Nay, verily He encompasses all things.
Hā mīm
‘ayn sīn qāf.
Thus does He reveal to you and to those [who were] before you, God, the Mighty, the Wise.
To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Exalted, the Tremendous.
The heavens are well-nigh rent asunder from above one another, and the angels glorify with praise of their Lord, and ask forgiveness for those on earth. Verily God is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
And those who have taken besides Him guardians, God is watchful over them; and you are not a guardian over them.

And thus have We revealed to you an Arabic Qur’ān, that you may warn the mother-town and those around it, and that you may warn of the Day of Gathering of which there is no doubt. A part will be in Paradise and a part will be in the Blaze.
And had God willed, He would have made them one community; but He admits whomever He will into His mercy, and the evildoers have neither guardian nor helper.
Or have they taken guardians besides Him? But God, He [alone] is the Guardian, and He revives the dead, and He has power over all things.
And whatever you may differ in, the verdict therein belongs to God. That then is God, my Lord; in Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn penitently.

The Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you, from your own selves, pairs, and [also] pairs of the cattle: He multiplies you by such [means]. There is nothing like Him. He is the Heare, the Seer.
To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision for whomever He will, and He restricts [it]. Truly He has knowledge of all things.

He has prescribed for you as a religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus [declaring], ‘Establish religion and do not be divided in it’. Dreadful is for the idolaters that to which you summon them. God chooses for it whomever He will, and He guides to it whomever turns penitently.

And they did not become divided, except after the knowledge had come to them, out of [jealous] rivalry among themselves. And were it not for a Word that preceded from your Lord, until an appointed term, it would have [already] been judged between them. And indeed those who were made heirs to the Scripture after them are truly in grave doubt concerning him.

So to that then summon and be upright, just as you have been commanded, and do not follow them in their desires. And say: ‘I believe in whatever Book God has revealed. And I have been commanded to be just between you. God is our Lord and your Lord. Our deeds concern us and your deeds concern you. There is no argument between us and you. God will bring us together, and to Him is the [final] destination’.

And those who argue concerning God after His call has been answered, their argument stands refuted with their Lord, and [His] wrath shall be upon them, and there will be a severe chastisement for them.
God it is Who has revealed the Book with the truth as well as the Balance. And what do you know — perhaps the Hour is near!

Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, but those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth. Nay, but verily those who are in doubt concerning the Hour are indeed in extreme error!
God is Gracious to His servants. He provides for whomever He will. And He is the Strong, the Mighty.

And whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will enhance for him his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him of it; but in the Hereafter he will have no share.

Or have they associates who have prescribed for them a religion which God has not given permission for? And were it not for a [prior] decisive word, it would have been judged between them. Truly the wrongdoers will have a painful chastisement.

You will see the wrongdoers apprehensive because of what they had earned; and it will surely befall them; but those who believe and perform righteous deeds will be in the lushest Gardens. They will have whatever they wish near their Lord; that is the great favour.

That is the good tidings which God gives to His servants who believe and perform righteous deeds. Say: ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it, except the affection for [my] kinsfolk. And whoever acquires a good deed, We shall enhance for him its goodness. Surely God is Forgiving, Appreciative.

Or do they say, ‘He has invented a lie against God?’ For if God will, He can seal your heart. And God will efface the falsehood and vindicate the truth with His words. Truly He is Knower of what is in the breasts.
And He it is Who accepts repentance from His servants, and pardons evil deeds, and knows what they do.
And He answers those who believe and perform righteous deeds, and He enhances them of His bounty. And as for the disbelievers, for them there will be a severe chastisement.
For were God to extend His provision to His servants, they would surely become covetous in the earth; but He sends down in the measure that He will. Surely He is Aware, Seer of His servants.
And He it is Who sends down the [saving] rain after they have despaired, and unfolds His mercy, and He is the [true] Patron, the Praised.
And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and whatever He has scattered in them in the way of creatures. And He is able to bring them together, whenever He will.
And whatever affliction may befall you is on account of what your [own] hands have earned. And He pardons much.
And you cannot escape on earth, and besides God you have neither protector nor helper.
And of His signs are the ships [that run] on the sea [appearing] like landmarks.
If He will He stills the wind, whereat they remain motionless on its surface. Surely in that there are signs for every steadfast, grateful [servant].
Or He wrecks them because of what they have earned. And He pardons much.
And that those who dispute concerning Our signs may know they have no refuge.
So whatever you have been given is [but] the enjoyment of the life of this world. But what is with God is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord,
and those who avoid grave sins and indecencies and [who], when they are angry, forgive,
and those who answer their Lord, and whose courses of action are [a matter of] counsel between them, and who, of what We have bestowed on them, expend,
and those who, when they suffer aggression defend themselves:
For the requital of an evil deed is an evil deed like it. But whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward will be with God. Truly He does not like wrongdoers.
And whoever defends himself after he has been wronged, for such, there will be no course [of action] against them.
A course [of action] is only [open] against those who wrong people and seek [to commit] in the earth what is not right. For such there will be a painful chastisement.
But verily he who is patient and forgives — surely that is [true] constancy in [such] affairs.
And whomever God leads astray has no protector after Him. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they sight the chastisement, saying, ‘Is there any way to return?’

And you will see them being exposed to it, submissive by abasement, looking with a furtive glance. And those who believe will say, ‘Verily the [true] losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Truly the wrongdoers will be in lasting chastisement.
And they have no guardians to help them besides God, and whomever God leads astray has no course [of action]’.
Answer your Lord before there comes a day for which there is no revoking from God. On that day you will have no refuge, and for you there will be no [way of] denying.

But if they are disregardful, We have not sent you as a keeper over them. Your duty is only to deliver the Message. And indeed when We let man taste from Us some mercy, he exults in it; but if some ill befalls them because of what their [own] hands have sent ahead, then lo! man is ungrateful.
To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He will; He gives to whomever He will females, and He gives to whomever He will males.
Or He combines them, males and females; and He makes whomever He will infertile. Surely He is Knower, Powerful.

And it is not [possible] for any human that God should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or that He should send a messenger, and he then reveals with His permission whatever He will. Truly He is Exalted, Wise.

And thus, have We revealed to you a Spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith; but We have made it a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants. And verily you guide to a straight path,
the path of God, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Surely with God all matters end [their journey].
Hā mīm.
By the Book that clarifies.
Lo! We have made it an Arabic Qur’ān that perhaps you may understand.
And it is indeed in the Mother Book, [which is] with Us [and it is] indeed exalted.
Shall We turn away from you the Remembrance, utterly because you are a profligate folk?
And how many a prophet did We send among the ancients!
And never did a prophet come to them but that they used to deride him.
So We destroyed those who were mightier than them in prowess, and [already] there passed the example of the ancients.
And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘The Mighty, the Knower created them’.
He Who made the earth a cradle for you, and placed for you therein ways, that perhaps you may be guided,
and Who sent down water from the heaven in measure, and We revived with it a dead land. Thus will you be brought forth,
and Who created the pairs all of them, and made for you ships and cattle on which you ride,

that you may sit upon their backs; and then remember your Lord’s grace when you are settled on them, and say, ‘Glory be to Him Who has disposed this for us, and we [by] ourselves were no match for it.
And indeed it is to our Lord that we shall return’.
And they assign to Him from among His own servants a part. Man is verily a manifest ingrate.
Or He has adopted, from all that He has created daughters, and preferred you with sons?
And when one of them is given the good tidings of that which he has attributed to the Compassionate One, his face becomes darkened, and he chokes inwardly.
What! one that is brought up amid trinkets and is incoherent in a dispute?
And they have made the angels, who are themselves servants of the Compassionate One, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be written down and they will be questioned.
And they say, ‘Had the Compassionate One [so] willed, we would not have worshipped them’. They do not have any knowledge of that; and they are only surmising.
Or have We brought them a scripture before, so that they are holding fast to it?
Nay, but they say, ‘Lo! we found our fathers following a [certain] creed and we are indeed in their footsteps to be guided’.

And thus We never sent a warner before you into any city without that its affluent folk said: ‘Lo! we found our fathers following a [certain] creed and [so] we are indeed following in their footsteps’.
Say: ‘What! even if I bring you a better [means to] guidance than what you found your fathers following?’ They say, ‘Lo! we disbelieve in what you are sent with’.
So We took vengeance on them; behold then how was the sequel for the deniers.
And when Abraham said to his father and his people, ‘Surely I am innocent of that which you worship,
except Him Who originated me; for He will indeed guide me’.
And he made it a word enduring among his posterity that perhaps they might recant.
Nay, but I have let these and their fathers enjoy [life] until there came to them the truth, and a messenger who makes [things] clear.
But when the truth came to them, they said, ‘This is sorcery, and we are indeed disbelievers in it’.
And they said, ‘If only this Qur’ān had been revealed to some great man from the two towns!’

Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others by degrees, so that some of them may take others in service, and the mercy of your Lord is better than what they amass.

And were it not [for the danger] that mankind would be one community, We would have made, for those who disbelieve in the Compassionate One, roofs of silver for their houses and stairs by which they ascend,
and doors for their houses, and couches on which they recline,
and ornaments. Yet surely all that would be nothing but the [transient] enjoyment of the life of this world, and the Hereafter with your Lord is for the God-fearing.
And whoever withdraws from the Remembrance of the Compassionate One, We assign for him a devil and he becomes his companion.
And indeed they bar them from the way, while they suppose that they are [rightly] guided,
until when he comes to Us, he says: ‘O would that there were between me and you the distance of the two easts!’ — What an evil companion then!
And it will not benefit you this day, given that you did wrong that you will be sharing in the chastisement.
Can you, then, make the deaf hear, or can you guide the blind and one who is in manifest error?
So if We take you away, then We will take vengeance on them,
or We show you that which We have promised them, for surely We have power over them.
So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you; surely you are on a straight path.
And it is indeed a Reminder for you and for your people. And you will [eventually] be questioned.
And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: Did We [ever] appoint, besides the Compassionate One, gods to be worshipped?
And verily We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his council, and he said, ‘I am indeed the messenger of the Lord of the Worlds’.
But when he brought them Our signs, behold! they laughed at them.
And We never showed them a sign, but it was greater than the one before it. And We seized them with chastisement, that perhaps they might recant.
And they said, ‘O sorcerer! supplicate your Lord for us by the covenant that He has made with you. Assuredly we will be guided’.
But as soon as We relieved them from the chastisement, behold! they had broken their pledge.
And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, ‘O my people, does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not perceive?
Or am I not better than this one, who is contemptible, and who can scarcely speak clearly?
Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast on him or the angels not come with him one after the other?’
Thus did he persuade his people and they obeyed him. They were truly an immoral folk.
So when they had angered Us, We took vengeance on them and drowned them all.
And We made them a thing past, and an example for others.
And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold! your people laugh at it.
And they say, ‘Are our gods better or he?’ They only cite this to you for the sake of contention. Nay, but they are a contentious lot.
He is only a servant [of Ours] on whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an exemplar for the Children of Israel.
And had We willed, We would have appointed among you angels to be [your] successors in the earth.
And indeed he is a portent of the Hour so do not doubt it but: ‘Follow me. This is a straight path’.
And do not let Satan bar you. Indeed he is a manifest enemy of yours.
And when Jesus came with the clear signs, he said, ‘Verily I have brought you wisdom, and [I have come] to make clear to you some of what you are at variance over. So fear God and obey me.
Assuredly God is my Lord and your Lord; so worship Him — that is a straight path’.
But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who do wrong from the chastisement of a painful day.
Are they awaiting anything, but that Hour should come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware?
Friends will, on that day, be foes of one another, except for the God-fearing.
‘O My servants, there is no fear for you this day, nor will you grieve,
those who believed in Our signs and had submitted themselves [to Me].
Enter Paradise, you and your spouses to be made joyful.
They will be served from all around with [large] dishes of gold and goblets and therein will be whatever souls desire and eyes delight in, and you will abide in it [forever].
And that is the Paradise which you have been given to inherit [as the reward] for what you used to do.
Therein are abundant fruits for you, from which you will eat’.
Indeed the guilty will abide [forever] in the chastisement of Hell —
it will not be lightened for them and they will be [utterly] despondent in it.
And We never wronged them, but they themselves were the wrongdoers.
And they will call out, ‘O Mālik, let your Lord finish us off!’ He will say, ‘You will surely remain!’
‘Verily We brought you the truth, but most of you were averse to the truth’.
Or have they contrived some matter? For We [too] are indeed contriving.
Or do they reckon that We do not hear their secret thoughts and their conspiring? Yes indeed! and Our messengers are with them keeping a record.
Say: ‘If the Compassionate One had a son, I would have been first among the worshippers.
Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne above what they allege!’
So leave them to indulge and play, until they encounter that day of theirs which they are promised.
And He it is Who in the heaven is God, and in the earth is God; and He is the Wise, the Knower.
And Blessed be He to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them; and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him they will [all] be returned.
And those whom they call on besides Him have no power of intercession, except those who bear witness to the truth with [full] knowledge.
And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, ‘God’. How can they then deviate?
And [as] for his saying: ‘O my Lord! These are indeed a people who have no faith’.
Then disregard them and say, ‘Peace!’ For they will [soon] come to know.
Hā mīm.
By the Book that clarifies.
Indeed We revealed it on a blessed night. Indeed We have been warning.
In it every definitive matter is distinguished.
As an ordinance from Us. Indeed We have been sending from your Lord,
as a mercy. Surely He is the Hearer, the Knower.
Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them if you should be certain.
There is no god except Him. He gives life and brings death. Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.
Nay, but they linger in doubt, playing.
So watch out for the day when the heaven will produce a visible smoke.
that will envelop the people: ‘This is a painful chastisement!
Our Lord, relieve us from the chastisement; indeed we have believed’.
How can there be a reminder for them, when already there has come to them a manifest Messenger,
but they turned away from him and said, ‘He has been taught; [he is] a madman!’
‘Indeed We will remove the chastisement a little. [But] you will indeed revert!’
The day when We shall assault with the most mighty assault; [then] indeed We shall take vengeance.
And certainly We tried before them the people of Pharaoh, when a messenger came to them, who was honoured,
and, ‘Do not rebel against God. Lo! I bring you a clear warrant’.
‘And truly I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you should stone me.
And if you do not believe me, then stay away from me’.
So he called to his Lord, saying, ‘These are indeed a guilty lot!’
‘Then set out with My servants by night; for you will assuredly be pursued.
And leave the sea behind at rest: indeed they will be a drowned host’.
How many gardens and fountains did they leave behind,
as well as sown fields and many a glorious residence,
and the bounty in which they rejoiced!
So [it was] and We made these an inheritance for another people.
So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them; nor were they reprieved.
And verily We delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating chastisement,
from Pharaoh. Truly he was a tyrant of the wanton ones.
And verily We chose them with a knowledge over [all] the worlds.
And We gave them signs in which there was a manifest trial.
Indeed these ones say,
‘It is nothing more than our first death, and we shall not be resurrected.
Bring us then our fathers, if you are being truthful’.
Are they better, or the people of Tubba’ and those before them? We destroyed [them]; indeed they were criminals.
And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, [intending] to play.
We did not create them, except with the truth; but most of them do not know.
Assuredly the Day of Decision will be the tryst for all of them,
the day when a friend will not avail a friend anything, nor will they be helped,
except for him on whom God has mercy. He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.
Lo! the tree of Zaqqūm
will be the food of the sinful.
Like molten copper it will boil inside the bellies,
as the boiling of boiling water.
‘Seize him and drag him to the midst of Hell-fire.
Then pour over his head the torture of boiling water!’
‘Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble one!
This is indeed that which you used to doubt’.
Assuredly the God-fearing will be in a secure place,
amid gardens and springs,
dressed in fine silk and [heavy] silk brocade, sitting face to face.
So [shall it be]; and We shall pair them with houris of beautiful eyes.
They will call therein every fruit, [remaining] secure.
They will not taste death therein, other than the first death. And He will shield them from the chastisement of Hell-fire —
a bounty from your Lord. That is the supreme triumph.
For We have made it easy in your tongue that perhaps they may remember.
So be on the look out. Indeed they [too] are on the look out.
Hā mīm.
The revelation of the Book is from God, the Mighty, the Wise.
Truly in the heavens and the earth there are signs for believers.
And in your creation, and what He has scattered of animals, there are signs for a people who are certain;

and the alternation of night and day, and what God sends down from the heaven [in the way] of provision with which He revives the earth after it is dead, and the circulation of the winds, there are signs for a people who understand.
These are the signs of God which We recite to you with truth. So in what [kind of] discourse then, after God and His signs will they believe?
Woe to every sinful liar,
who hears the signs of God being recited to him, then persists arrogantly, as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful chastisement.
And should he come to know anything of Our signs, he takes them in mockery. For such there is a degrading chastisement.
Beyond them is Hell, and that which they have earned will not avail them in any way, nor those whom they took besides God as patrons. And for them there will be a great chastisement.
This is a guidance, and those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them there will be a torture of a painful chastisement.
God it is Who disposed for you the sea so that the ships may sail upon it by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and that perhaps you may give thanks.
And He has disposed for you whatever is in the heavens, and whatever is in the earth, all being from Him. Surely in that there are signs for a people who reflect.
Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not anticipate the days of God that He may requite a people for what they used to earn.
Whoever acts righteously, it is for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is to the detriment thereof; then to your Lord you will be returned.
And verily We gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, and [the means of] judgement, and prophethood, and We provided them with the good things, and We favoured them above [all] worlds.

And We gave them clear illustrations of the commandment. And they did not differ, except after the knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ.
Then We set you upon a [clear] course of the commandment; so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.
Assuredly they will not avail you in any way against God. And assuredly the wrongdoers are allies of one another; but God is the ally [only] of the God-fearing.
This is [a set of] insights for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who have certainty.

Or do those who have perpetrated evil acts suppose that We shall treat them as those who believe and perform righteous deeds, equally in their life and in their death? How evil is that judgement which they make!
And God created the heavens and the earth with the truth and so that every soul may be requited for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.

Have you then seen him who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and whom God has led astray knowingly, and set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and laid a covering over his sight? So who will guide him after God? Will you not then remember?
And they say, ‘There is only our life in this world. We die and we live, and nothing but time destroys us’. Of that they have no knowledge; they are only making conjectures.
And when Our signs, are recited to them, being clear signs, their only argument is to say, ‘Bring us our fathers, if you are being truthful’.
Say: ‘God [is the One Who] gives you life, then makes you die, then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection, in which there is no doubt; but most people do not know’.
And to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And on the day when the Hour sets in on that day the followers of falsehood will be losers.
And you will see every community. Every community will be summoned to its record: ‘Today you will be requited for what you used to do.
This is Our book, which pronounces against you with truth. Indeed We used to write down what you used to do’.
So as for those who believed and performed righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the manifest triumph.
But as for those who disbelieved: ‘Were not My signs recited to you, but you were disdainful and were a guilty lot?
And when it was said: “God’s promise is indeed true, and there is no doubt about the Hour”, you said, “We do not know what the Hour is. We only make conjectures and we are by no means certain” ’.
And there will appear before them the evils of what they did, and they will be besieged by what they used to deride.
And it will be said: ‘Today We will forget you, just as you forgot the encounter of this day of yours, and your abode will be the Fire, and you will not have any helpers.
That is because you took God’s signs in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you’. So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they asked to make amends.
So to God belongs [all] praise; Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, the Lord of the Worlds.
And to Him belongs [all] grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.
Hā mīm.
The revelation of the Book is from God, the Mighty, the Wise.
We have not created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except in truth, and for an appointed term. Yet those who disbelieve are disregardful of what they are warned.

Say: ‘Have you considered what you invoke besides God? Show me what they have created of the earth. Or do they have any share in the heavens? Bring me a scripture before this or some vestige of knowledge if you are truthful’.
And who is further astray than him who invokes such as would not respond to him [even] until the Day of Resurrection and who are heedless of their supplication?
And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them and they will deny their worship.
And when Our signs are recited to them, being clear signs, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, ‘This is plain sorcery!’

Or do they say, ‘He has invented it?’ Say: ‘If I have invented it, still you would have no power to avail me against God in any way. He knows best what you delve into [of gossip] concerning it. He suffices as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful’.
Say: ‘I am not a novelty among the messengers. Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me. And I am only a plain warner’.

Say: ‘Have you considered? if it is from God and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has [already] testified to the like of it, and he has believed [in it], while you act with arrogance …’. Truly God does not guide wrongdoing folk’.

And those who disbelieve say of those who believe: ‘Had it been [anything] good, they would not have attained it before us’. And since they will not be guided by it, they say, ‘This is an ancient lie!’
Yet before it, [there was] the Book of Moses, as a guidepost and a mercy, and this is a Book that confirms in the Arabic tongue to warn those who do wrong, and [as] good tidings for the virtuous.
Assuredly those who say, ‘Our Lord is God’ and then remain upright, no fear will befall them, nor will they grieve.
Those will be the inhabitants of Paradise, abiding therein as a reward for what they used to do.

And We have enjoined man to be kind to his parents. His mother carries him in travail, and gives birth to him in travail, and his gestation and his weaning take thirty months. So that when he is mature and reaches forty years he says, ‘My Lord! Inspire me to give thanks for Your favour with which You have favoured me and my parents, and that I may act righteously in a way that will please You, and invest my seed with righteousness. Indeed I repent to You and I am truly of those who submit [to You]’.
Those are they from whom We accept the best of what they do, and overlook their misdeeds, [as they stand] among the inhabitants of Paradise — [this is] the true promise which they were promised.

As for him who says to his parents: ‘Fie on you both. Do you threaten me that I shall be raised, when already generations have passed away before me?’ And they call on God for succour, ‘Woe to you. Believe! Surely God’s promise is true’. But he says, ‘This is nothing but the fables of the ancients’.
Such are the ones against whom the Word is due concerning communities of jinn and humans that have passed away before them. Truly they are losers.
And for each one there will be degrees [of status], according to what they have done, and that He may recompense them fully for their deeds, and they will not be wronged.

And on the day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire: ‘You squandered your good things during your life of the world and enjoyed them. So today you will be requited with the chastisement of humiliation in return for acting arrogantly in the earth without right and in return for that regarding which you used to act immorally’.

And mention the brother of ‘ād when he warned his people at Ahqāf and already warners had passed away before him and after him, saying, ‘Do not worship anyone but God. Truly I fear for you the chastisement of a dreadful day’.
They said, ‘Have you come to divert us from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful’.
He said, ‘The knowledge is with God only, and I am [merely] conveying to you what I have been sent with. But I see that you are an ignorant lot’.

Then, when they saw it as a sudden cloud heading towards their valleys, they said, ‘This is a cloud that will bring us rain!’ Nay, but it is what you sought to hasten a hurricane containing a painful chastisement,
destroying everything by the command of its Lord. So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thu do We requite guilty folk.

And verily We had empowered them in ways in which We have not empowered you, and We had vested them with ears and eyes and hearts. But their ears and their eyes and their hearts did not avail them in any way since they used to deny the signs of God, and they were besieged by what they used to deride.
And We certainly destroyed the towns [that were] around you, and We dispensed the signs so that perhaps they might return.
So why did they not help them, those whom they had chosen besides God, as [a means of] nearness, to be gods? Nay, but they forsook them and that was their lie and what they used to invent.

And when We sent a company of jinn your way to listen to the Qur’ān and, when they were in its presence, they said: ‘Listen carefully!’ Then, when it was finished, they went back to their people to warn [them].
They said, ‘O our people! Indeed we have heard a Book which has been revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it. It guides to the truth and to a straight way.
O our people! Respond to God’s summoner, and believe in him, and He will forgive you some of your sins and shelter you from a painful chastisement.
And whoever does not respond to God’s summoner cannot thwart God on earth, and he will not have, besides Him, any protectors — those are in manifest error’.
Have they not seen that God, Who created the heavens and the earth and [Who] was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed. Indeed He has is able to do all things.

And on the day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire: ‘Is not this the truth?’ They will say, ‘Yes, by our Lord!’ He will say, ‘Then taste the chastisement for what you used to disbelieve [in]’.

So endure [with patience] just as the resolute from among the messengers endured [with patience]. And do not seek to hasten [it] for them. It shall seem for them, on the day when they see what they are promised, as though they had tarried, only an hour of a day. A communication. So shall any be destroyed, but the immoral folk?
Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God, He will leave their works to waste.

But those who believe and perform righteous deeds and believe in what has been revealed to Muhammad — and it is the truth from their Lord — He will absolve them of their misdeeds and rightly dispose their mind.
That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and because those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus, does God strike for mankind similitudes of themselves.

So when you encounter [in battle] those who disbelieve, then [attack them with] a striking of the necks. Then, when you have made thoroughly decimated them, bind. Thereafter either [set them free] by grace or by ransom, until the war lay down its burdens. So [shall it be]. And had God wished, He could have [Himself] taken vengeance on them, but that He may test some of you by means of others. And those who are slain in the way of God, He will not let their works go to waste.
He will guide them and rightly dispose their minds.
And He will admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them.
O you who believe! If you help God, He will help you and make your foothold firm.
And as for those who disbelieve, wretchedness shall be their lot. And He will make their works go to waste.
That is because they are averse to what God has revealed, so He has made their works fail.
Have they not travelled in the land to see the nature of the consequence for those who were before them? God destroyed them; and [a fate] the like thereof will be for the disbelievers.
That is because God is Patron of those who believe and because the disbelievers have no patron.

God will surely admit those who believe and perform righteous deeds into gardens underneath which rivers flow. As for those who disbelieve, they take their enjoyment and eat as the cattle eat; and the Fire will be their habitation.
And how many a town mightier in power than your town, which expelled you, have We destroyed, and they had none to help them.
Is he who follows a clear sign from his Lord like those whose evil deeds have been adorned for them, and who follow their desires?

A similitude of the Garden promised to the God-fearing: therein are rivers of unstaling water, and rivers of milk unchanging in flavour, and rivers of wine delicious to the drinkers, and [also] rivers of purified honey; and there will be for them therein every fruit and forgiveness from their Lord. [Is such a one] like him who abides in the Fire? And they will be given to drink boiling water which rips apart their bowels.

And there are some among them who listen to you, until, when they go forth from you, they say to those who have been given knowledge: ‘What was he saying just now?’ Those are the ones on whose hearts God has set a seal and who follow their own desires.
But those who are [rightly] guided, He enhances their guidance and invests them with fear [of Him].
Do they, then, await anything except that the Hour should come upon them suddenly? For already its portents have come. So, when it has come upon them, for what [benefit] will their reminder be?
Know, then, that there is no god except God, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And God knows your going to and fro and your place of rest.

And those who believe say: ‘Why has a sūra not been revealed?’ But when a definitive sūra is revealed, and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is a sickness, looking at you with the look of someone fainting at [the point of] death. Yet more fitting for them
would be [to offer] obedience and honourable words. Then, when the matter has been resolved upon if they are loyal to God, it will be better for them.
May it not be [the case] with you that if you were to turn away, you would then cause corruption in the land and sever your kinship ties?
Those are the ones whom God has cursed, so made them deaf and blinded their eyes.
Do they not contemplate the Qur’ān? Or is it that there are locks on, [their] hearts?
Truly those who have turned their backs after the guidance has become clear to them, Satan has seduced them and has given them [false] hopes.
That is because they said to those who were averse to what God revealed: ‘We will obey you in some matters’; and God knows their secrets.
Then how will it be when the angels take them away, beating their faces and their backs?
That is because they followed what angers God, and [because] they were averse to what pleases Him. Therefore He has made their works fail.
Or did those in whose hearts is a sickness suppose that God would not expose their rancour?
And if We will, We could show them to you, then you would recognise them by their mark. And you will certainly recognise them by [their] tone of speech, and God knows your deeds.
And We will assuredly try you until We know those of you who struggle [for God’s cause] and those who are steadfast, and We will appraise your record.
Indeed those who disbelieve and bar from way of God, and defy the Messenger after the guidance has become clear to them, they will not hurt God in any way, and He will make their works fail.
O you who believe! Obey God and obey the Messenger, and do not render your own works void.
Indeed those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God, and then die as disbelievers, God will never forgive them.
So do not falter, and [do not] call for peace when you have the upper hand, and God is with you, and He will not stint you in [the reward for] your works.
The life of this world is merely play and diversion; but if you believe and are wary, He will give you your rewards, and will not ask you your wealth [in return].
If He were to ask you for it, and press you, you would be niggardly, and this would expose your rancour.

Lo! there you are those who are being called to expend in the way of God; yet among you there are those who are niggardly; and whoever is niggardly is niggardly only to his own soul. For God is the Independent One, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you.
Verily We have given you a clear victory,
that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come, and that He may perfect His favour to you and guide you to a straight path,
and that God may grant you a mighty victory.

He it is Who sent down the spirit of Peace into the hearts of the believers, that they might add faith to their faith. And to God belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth. And God is ever Knower, Wise;

so that He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide, and that He may absolve them of their misdeeds; for that, in God’s sight, is a supreme triumph;

and so that He may chastise the hypocrites, men and women, and the idolaters, men and women, and those who make evil assumptions about God. For them will be an evil turn of fortune, and God is wroth with them, and He has cursed them, and has prepared for them Hell — and it is an evil destination!
And to God belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth; and God is ever Mighty, Wise.
Indeed We have sent you as a witness, and a bearer of good tidings, and a warner,
that you may believe in God and His Messenger, and that you may support Him, and revere Him, and glorify Him morning and evening.

Truly those who pledge allegiance to you, in fact pledge allegiance to God. The Hand of God is above their hands. So whoever reneges, reneges against his own soul; and whoever fulfils the covenant which he has made with God, He will give him a great reward.

Those of the Bedouins who were left behind, will say to you, ‘Our possessions and our families kept us occupied. So ask forgiveness for us!’ They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say: ‘Who can avail you anything against God should He desire to cause you harm or desire to bring you benefit? Nay, but God is ever Aware of what you do.

Nay, but you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that [thought] was adorned in your hearts, and you thought evil thoughts, and you were a ruined lot’.
And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze.
And to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth: He forgives whomever He will and chastises whomever He will; and God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.

Those who were left behind will say, when you set forth after spoils, in order to capture them, ‘Let us follow you’. They desire to change the words of God. Say: ‘You shall never follow us! Thus has God said beforehand’. Then they will say, ‘Nay, but you are envious of us’. Nay, but they never understood, [all] except a few.

Say to those of the Bedouins who were left behind: ‘You shall be called against a people possessed of great might, you shall fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey God will give you a good reward; but if you turn away like you turned away before, He will chastise you with a painful chastisement’.

There is no blame on the blind, nor [is there] blame on the lame, nor [is there] blame on the sick. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens underneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away, him He will chastise with a painful chastisement.

Verily God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. And He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down the spirit of Peace upon them, and rewarded them with a near victory,
and abundant spoils which they will capture, and God is ever Mighty, Wise.

God has promised you abundant spoils which you will capture. So He has expedited this one for you, and withheld men’s hands from you, so that it may be a sign for the believers, and that He may guide you on a straight path;
and others which you were not able to capture, God has verily encompassed these [already]. And God has power over all things.
And if those who disbelieve had fought you, they would have turned their backs [to flee] — then they would not have found any protector or helper.
And it is He Who withheld their hands from you, and your hands from them, in the valley of Mecca after He had made you victors over them. And God is ever Seer of what you do.

They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and [prevented] the offering which was detained from reaching its destination. And were it not for [some of] the believing men and believing women, whom you did not know, lest you should trample them, and thus incur sin on account of them without knowing, so that God may admit into His mercy whom He will. Had they been clearly separated, We would have surely chastised the disbelievers among them with a painful chastisement.

When those who disbelieve nourished in their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of pagandom, [but] then God sent down His spirit of Peace upon His Messenger and the believers, and He made them abide by the word of God-fearing, for they were worthier of it, and deserving of it. And God is ever Knower of all things.

Verily God has fulfilled the vision for His Messenger in all truth: ‘You will assuredly enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in safety, to shave your heads, or to shorten [your hair], without any fear’. So He knew what you did not know, and assigned [you] before that a near victory.
It is He Who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion. And God suffices as witness:

Muhammad is the Messenger of God and those who are with him are hard against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing, prostrating [in worship]. They seek bounty from God and beatitude. Their mark from the effect of prostration. That is their description in the Torah and their description in the Gospel is as a seed that sends forth its shoot and strengthens it, and it grows stout and rises firmly upon its stalk, delighting the sowers, so that He may enrage the disbelievers by them. God has promised those of them who believe and perform righteous deeds, forgiveness and a great reward.
O you who believe, do not venture ahead of God and His Messenger, and fear God. Surely God is Hearer, Knower.
O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not shout words at him, as you shout to one another, lest your works should be invalidated without your being aware.
Truly those who lower their voices in the presence of God’s Messenger — they are the ones whose hearts God has tested for God-fearing. For them will be forgiveness and a great reward
Truly those who call you from behind the apartments — most of them do not understand.
And had they been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them; and God is Forgiving, Merciful.
O you who believe, if a reprobate should come to you with some tiding, verify [it], lest you injure a folk out of ignorance; and then become remorseful of what you have perpetrated.

And know that the Messenger of God is among you. If he were to obey you in many matters, you would surely be in trouble. But God has endeared faith to you, adorning your hearts with it, and He has made odious to you disbelief and immorality and disobedience. Those they are the right-minded;

And if two parties of believers fall to fighting, make peace between them. And if one of them aggresses against the other, fight the one which aggresses until it returns to God’s ordinance. Then, if it returns, reconcile them, and act justly. Surely God loves the just.
The believers are indeed brothers. Therefore [always] make peace between your brethren, and fear God, so that perhaps you might receive mercy.

O you who believe, do not let any people deride another people: who may be better than they are; nor let any women deride [other] women who may be better than they are. And do not defame one another, nor insult one another by nicknames. Evil is the name of immorality after faith! And whoever does not repent, those — they are the evildoers.

O you who believe, shun much suspicion. Indeed some suspicions are sins. And do not spy, nor backbite one another. Would any of you love to eat the flesh of his brother dead? You would abhor it. And fear God; assuredly God is Relenting, Merciful.

O mankind! We have indeed created you from a male and a female, and made you nations and tribes that you may come to know one another. Truly the noblest of you in the sight of God is the most God-fearing among you. Truly God is Knower, Aware.

The Bedouins say, ‘We believe’. Say: ‘You do not believe; but rather say, “We have submitted”; for faith has not yet entered into your hearts’. Yet if you obey God and His Messenger, He will not diminish for you anything of your deeds. God is indeed Forgiving, Merciful.
The [true] believers are only those who believe in God and His Messenger, and then have not doubted, and who strive with their wealth and their souls for the cause of God. It is they who are sincere.
Say: ‘Do you [pretend to] inform God about your religion, when God knows all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, and [even though] God is Knower of all things?’

They deem it to be a favour to you that they have submitted. Say: ‘Do not deem your submission to be a favour to me. Rather, it is God Who has done you a favour in that He has guided you to faith, if you are being sincere.
Truly God knows the Unseen of the heavens and the earth, and God is Seer of what you do’.
Qāf. By the glorious Qur’ān.
Nay, but they consider it odd that there should have come to them a warner from among themselves. So the disbelievers say, ‘This is an odd thing!
What! When we are dead and have become dust? That is a far-fetched return!’
We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserving Book.
Nay, but they denied the truth, when it came to them and so they are [now] in a confounded situation.
Have they not then looked at the heaven above them, how We have built it, and adorned it, and how there are no cracks in it?
And the earth We have spread it out, and cast in it firm mountains, and caused every delightful kind to grow in it,
as an insight and a reminder for every penitent servant.
And We send down from the heaven blessed water with which We cause to grow gardens and the grain that is harvested,
and the date-palms that stand tall with piled spathes,
as provision for [Our] servants; and with it We revive a dead land. So shall be the rising.
The people of Noah denied before them and [so did] the dwellers at al-Rass and Thamūd,
and ‘ād, and Pharaoh, the brethren of Lot,
and the dwellers in the wood, and the people of Tubba’. Each denied the messengers, and so My threat became due.
Were We then wearied by the first creation? Nay, yet they are in doubt about a new creation.
And verily We created man and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
When the two Receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left,
he does not utter a word but that there is beside him a watcher, [who is] ready.
And the agony of death arrives with the truth. That is what you used to shun.
And the Trumpet will be blown. That is the Day of the Promised Threat.
And every soul will come, accompanied by a driver, and a witness:
‘Verily, you were oblivious of this: So [now] We have removed from you your covering, and so your sight on this day is acute’.
And his companion will say, ‘This is what I have ready with me [as testimony]’:
‘Cast into Hell every obdurate disbeliever,
hinderer of good, transgressor, skeptic,
who has set up alongside God another god! Cast him then into the severe chastisement’.
And his companion will say, ‘Our Lord! I did not make him a rebel, but he [himself] was in extreme error’.
He will say, ‘Do not dispute in My presence, for I had already given you the threat.
The word [that comes] from Me cannot be altered, and I am not unjust to servants’
on the day when We will say to Hell, ‘Are you [now] full?’ and it will say: ‘Are there any more?’
And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing, not far [anymore].
‘This is what you were promised — [it is] for every penitent one, who is mindful,
who fears the Compassionate One [while He is] in the Unseen, and comes with a penitent heart’.
‘Enter it in peace! That is the day of immortality’.
Therein they will have whatever they wish; and with Us there is yet more.
And how many a generation We destroyed before them, who were mightier than these in prowess, and [who] then searched throughout the land [wondering]: is there any escape?
Assuredly there is in that a reminder for him who has a heart, or gives ear in [full] witness.
And verily We created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in six days, and no weariness touched Us.
So endure [patiently] what they say, and glorify with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before the sunset;
and glorify Him at [some part of the] night and after prostrations.
And listen on the day when the caller calls out from a place that is near.
On the day when they hear the Call of truth; that is the day of coming forth.
Indeed it is We Who give life and bring death, and to Us is the journey’s end.
On the day when the earth is split asunder from them, [they will come] hastening forth. That is an easy gathering for Us.
We know best what they say, and you are not [to be] a coercer of them. So admonish by the Qur’ān those who fear My threat.
By the scatterers that scatter
and those that bear a burden
and those that run with ease
and those that apportion by command,
assuredly what you are promised is true,
and assuredly judgement will take place!
And by the heaven with all its tracks,
indeed you are of differing opinions.
He is turned away therefrom who has deviated.
Perish the conjecturers,
who are in a stupor, heedless.
They ask: ‘When is the Day of Judgement?’
On the day when they will be tormented in the Fire:
‘Taste this torment of yours. This is what you sought to hasten on!’
Truly the God-fearing will be amid gardens and springs,
receiving what their Lord has given them, for indeed formerly they had been virtuous.
Little of the night did they use to sleep,
and at dawns they used to seek forgiveness,
and there was a share in their wealth [assigned] for the beggar and the deprived.
And in the earth there are signs for those who know with certainty,
and in your souls. Will you not then perceive?
And in the heaven is your provision, and [there is also] what you are promised.
So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is as assuredly true as [the fact] that you have [power of] speech.
Has the story reached you of Abraham’s honoured guests?
When they entered upon him and said, ‘Peace!’ He said, ‘Peace!’ [These are] an unfamiliar folk.
Then he went aside to his family and brought a fat calf;
and he placed it near them saying, ‘Will you not eat?’
Then he conceived a fear of them. They said, ‘Do not be afraid!’ And they gave him good tidings of [the birth of] a knowledgeable boy.
Then his wife came forward clamouring and smote her face, and said, ‘A barren old woman!’
They said, ‘So has your Lord said. Indeed He is the Wise, the Knower’.
He said, ‘So what is your business, O you who have been sent [by God]?’
They said, ‘Lo! we have been sent to a guilty folk
that we may unleash upon them stones of clay,
marked by your Lord for [the destruction of] the prodigal’.
So We brought forth those in them who were believers,
but We did not find therein other than one house of those who had submitted [to God].
And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful chastisement.
And [a sign too] in Moses when We sent him to Pharaoh with a clear warrant,
but he turned away to his supports, saying, ‘A sorcerer, or a madman!’
So We seized him and his hosts and cast them into the waters, for he was blameworthy.
And [also] in ‘ād [was another sign], when We unleashed against them a barren wind.
It did not leave anything that it came upon without making it like decayed bones.
And [also] in Thamūd, when it was said to them, ‘Enjoy [yourselves] for a while!’
Then they defied the command of their Lord; so the thunderbolt seized them as they were looking around.
So they were unable to rise up, nor were they victors.
And the people of Noah aforetime. Indeed they were an immoral lot.
And the heaven, We built it with might, and indeed We are powerful.
And the earth, We spread it out: what excellent Spreaders then!
And of all things We created pairs that perhaps you might remember.
So flee unto God. Truly I am a clear warner to you from Him.
And do not set up another god alongside God. Truly I am a clear warner to you from Him.
Thus there did not come to those who were before them any messenger but they said: ‘A sorcerer, or a madman!’
Have they enjoined this upon one another? Nay, but they are an insolent folk.
So shun them, for you will not be reproached.
And remind for reminding truly benefits believers.
And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they may worship Me.
I do not desire from them any provision, nor do I desire that they should feed Me.
Indeed it is God Who is the Provider, the Lord of Strength, the Firm.
And for those who have wronged, there will assuredly be a lot like the lot of their counterparts. So let them not ask Me to hasten on.
For woe to those who disbelieve, from that day of theirs which they are promised.
By the Mount,
and an inscribed Book,
on an unrolled parchment.
By the [greatly] frequented House,
and the raised roof,
and the swarming sea:
lo! your Lord’s chastisement will assuredly take place;
there is none that can avert it.
On the day when the heaven will heave with a great heaving,
and the mountains move with a great motion.
Woe then on that day to the deniers,
those who play around in vain talk;
the day when they will be thrust with a violent thrust into Hell:
‘This is the Fire which you used to deny!
Is this then sorcery or is it that you do not see?
Burn in it! And whether you endure or do not endure will be the same for you. You are only being requited for what you used to do’.
Truly the God-fearing will be amid gardens and bliss,
rejoicing in what their Lord has given them, and [that] their Lord has shielded them from the chastisement of Hell-fire.
‘Eat and drink in full enjoyment [as a reward] for what you used to do’.

And those who believed and whom We made to be followed by their descendants in faith, We will make their descendants join them, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every man is subject to what he has earned.
And We will supply them with fruits and meat, such as they desire.
They will pass from one to another therein, a cup wherein is neither vain talk nor cause for sin.
And there will circulate from all around them youths of their own, as if they were hidden pearls.
And some among them will turn to one another, questioning each other.
They say: ‘Truly, before, amid our families, we used to be ever anxious;
but God showed us favour and shielded us from the piercing chastisement,
indeed before we used to call on Him. Verily He is the Benign, the Merciful.
So remind. For by the grace of your Lord you are neither soothsayer nor madman.
Or do they say: ‘A poet, for whom we may await the accidents of fate?’
Say: ‘Await! For I too will be with you awaiting’.
Or do their faculties of understanding prompt them to [say] this? Or are they a rebellious lot?
Or do they say, ‘He has improvised it?’ Rather they do not believe.
Then let them bring a discourse like it, if they are truthful.
Or were they created out of nothing? Or are they the creators?
Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Nay, but they are not certain.
Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord? Or are they the ones in control?
Or do they have a ladder, whereby they eavesdrop? Then let their eavesdropper produce a manifest warrant.
Or does He have daughters, whereas you have sons?
Or are you asking them for a fee so that they are weighed down with debt?
Or do they have [access to] the Unseen so that they can write it down?
Or do they desire to outmanoeuvre? But those who disbelieve, they are the outmanoeuvred ones!
Or do they have a god other than God? Glory be to God [exalted is He] above any partners that they may ascribe!
And if they were to see a fragment of the heaven falling, they would say: ‘A heap of clouds!’
So leave them until they encounter that day of theirs in which they will be thunderstruck,
the day when their guile will avail them nothing and they will not be helped.
And assuredly for those who do wrong, there is a chastisement beyond that, but most of them do not know.
And submit patiently to the judgement of your Lord, for surely you fare before Our eyes. And glorify with praise of your Lord when you rise,
and glorify Him at night and at the receding of the stars.
By the Star when it sets,
your companion has neither gone astray, nor has he erred;
nor does he speak out of [his own] desire.
It is but a revelation that is revealed,
taught to him by one of awesome power,
possessed of vigour; and he stood upright,
when he was on the highest horizon.
Then he drew near and drew closer still,
until he was within the length of two bows away or [even] nearer,
whereat He revealed to His servant what he revealed.
The heart did not deny what he saw.
Will you then dispute with him concerning what he saw?
And verily he saw him another time,
by the Lote-tree of the Ultimate Boundary,
near which is the Garden of the Retreat,
when there shrouded the Lote-tree that which shrouded [it],
The eye did not swerve, nor did it go beyond [the bounds].
Verily he saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.
Have you considered al-Lāt and al-’Uzzā,
and Manāt, the third, the other?
Are you to have males, and He females?
That, then, would indeed be an unfair division!

These are nothing but names which you have named, you and your fathers. God has not revealed any warrant for them. They follow nothing but conjecture and that which [ignoble] souls desire, even though guidance has already come to them from their Lord.
Or shall man have whatever he wishes for?
Yet to God belong the Hereafter and the former [life].
And how many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession cannot avail in any way except after God gives permission for whomever He wills, and He is satisfied.
Truly those who do not believe in the Hereafter give the angels the names of females.
But they do not have any knowledge thereof. They follow nothing but conjecture, and indeed conjecture can never substitute for the truth.
So shun him who turns away from Our Remembrance, and desires nothing but the life of this world.
That is the full extent of their knowledge. Truly your Lord knows best those who have strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are [rightly] guided.
And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth that He may requite those who do evil for what they have done, and reward those who are virtuous with the best [reward].

Those who avoid grave sins and abominations, excepting lesser offences. Truly your Lord is of vast forgiveness. He knows you best [from the time] when He produced you from the earth, and when you were hidden [fetuses] in the bellies of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves. He knows best those who are God-fearing.
Did you see him who turned away,
and gave a little, and was then grudging?
Does he possess knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees?
Or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses,
and Abraham who fulfilled [his summons]
that no burdened soul shall bear the burden of another,
and that man shall have only what he [himself] strives for,
and that his endeavour will be seen,
then he will be rewarded for it with the fullest reward,
and that the ultimate end is toward your Lord,
and that it is He Who makes to laugh and makes to weep,
and that it is He Who brings death and gives life,
and that He [Himself] creates the two spouses, the male and the female,
from a drop [of semen] once it is emitted,
and that with Him rests the second genesis,
and that it is He Who enriches and grants possessions,
and that it is He Who is the Lord of Sirius,
and that He destroyed former ‘ād
and Thamūd sparing not;
and the people of Noah before that; indeed they were more unjust and more insolent;
and the Deviant [cities] He overturned
so that there covered them that which covered [them].
Then which of the bounties of your Lord do you dispute?
This is a warner [in the tradition] of the warners of old.
The Impending [Hour] is imminent.
None besides God can disclose it.
Do you then marvel at this discourse,
and laugh and not weep,
while you remain oblivious?
So prostrate to God and worship Him
The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split.
And if they see a sign, they turn away and say: ‘A powerful sorcery!’
And they denied and followed their own desires, and every matter will be settled.
And verily there has come to them such tidings as contain a deterrent,
wisdom [that is] far-reaching; but warnings are of no avail.
So turn away from them! On the day when the Summoner summons to an awful thing;
with their downcast looks they will emerge from the graves as though they were scattered locusts,
scrambling toward the Summoner. The disbelievers will say: ‘This is a hard day!’
The people of Noah denied before them. Thus they denied Our servant and said, ‘A madman!’, and he was reviled.
And so he invoked his Lord, [saying,] ‘I have been overcome, so help [me]!’
Then We opened the gates of the heaven with torrential waters,
and We made the earth burst forth with springs and the waters met for a purpose that was preordained.
And We bore him on one, [made] of planks and nails,
sailing before Our eyes, as retaliation for [the sake of] him who was rejected.
And verily We left it as a sign. So is there anyone who will remember?
How [dreadful] then were My chastisement and My warnings?
And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember. So is there anyone who remember?
‘ād denied. How then were My chastisement and My warnings?
Indeed We unleashed upon them a clamorous wind on a day of prolonged ill fortune,
tearing people away, as if they were trunks of uprooted palm-trees.
How then were My chastisement and My warnings?
And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember. So is there anyone who will remember?
Thamūd denied the warnings,
and they said, ‘Is it a mortal alone among us that we are to follow? Then indeed we would be in error and insanity!
Has the Reminder been cast upon him [alone] from among us? Nay, but he is a conceited liar.
‘They will know tomorrow who is the conceited liar.
Lo! We are sending the She-camel as a trial for them. So watch them and remain patient.
And inform them that the water is to be divided between them, every drinking will be attended’.
But they called their companion so he took and he hamstrung [her].
How then were My chastisement and My warnings?
Indeed We unleashed upon them a single Cry, and they became like the chaff of a corral builder.
And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember. So is there anyone who will remember?
The people of Lot denied the warnings.
Indeed We unleashed upon them a squall of pebbles, [all] except the family of Lot whom We delivered at dawn
as a grace from Us. So do We requite him who gives thanks.
And verily he had warned them of Our strike, but they disputed the warnings.
And they had even solicited of him his guests. So We blotted out their eyes. ‘So taste [now] My chastisement and My warnings’.
And verily there greeted them in the early morning an abiding chastisement.
‘So taste [now] My chastisement and My warnings!’
And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember. So is there anyone who will remember?
And verily there came to Pharaoh’s folk the warnings.
They denied Our signs, all of them. So We seized them with the seizing of One [Who is] Mighty, Omnipotent.
Are your disbelievers better than those? Or have you [been granted] some immunity in the Scriptures?
Or do they say: ‘We are a host that will be helped to victory’?
The host will [truly] be routed and turn its back [to flee].
Nay, but the Hour is their tryst, and the Hour will be more calamitous and more bitter.
Indeed the guilty are in error and in a blazing fire.
The day when they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: ‘Taste [now] the touch of Saqar’.
Truly everything have We created in a measure.
And Our command is but a single word, like the twinkling of an eye.
And verily We have destroyed the likes of you. So is there anyone who will remember?
And everything they have done is in the scrolls,
and every small and great [thing] is inscribed.
Assuredly the God-fearing will be amid gardens and rivers
in an abode of truth, before a King [Who is] Omnipotent.
The Compassionate One
has taught the Qur’ān.
He created man,
teaching him the [coherent] speech.
The sun and the moon follow a reckoning,
and the grass and the trees prostrate.
And He has raised the heaven and set up the balance,
And observe the weights with justice and do not skimp the balance.
And the earth, He placed it for [all] creatures.
In it are fruits and date-palms with sheaths,
and grain with husk, and fragrant herb.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
He created man of dry clay resembling the potter’s,
and He created the jānn of a smokeless flame of fire.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Lord of the two Easts, and Lord of the two Wests.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
He has loosed the two waters; [and so] they meet.
Between them there is a barrier. They do not overstep.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
From [both of] them is brought forth the pearl and the coral.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
His are the crafted ships [that sail] in the sea [appearing] like landmarks.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Everyone who is on it will perish;
yet there will remain the countenance of your Lord, [the countenance] of majesty and munificence.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
All that is in the heavens and the earth implore Him. Every day He is upon some matter.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
We will attend to you, O you two heavy ones!
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
O company of jinn and humans, if you are able to pass through the confines of the heavens and the earth, then pass through! You will not pass through except with a sanction.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Against you will be unleashed a heat of fire and a flash of brass, and you will not be able to seek help.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
And when the heaven is split open, and it turns crimson like tanned leather.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Thus on that day no man will be questioned about his sin, nor any jinn.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
The guilty will be recognised by their mark; so they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
‘This is Hell which the guilty [were wont to] deny!’
They shall pass round between it and boiling hot water.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
But for those who feared the station of their Lord, there will be two gardens.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Both with [abundant] branches.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
In both of them there are two flowing springs.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
In both of them, of every fruit there are two kinds.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
In them are maidens of restrained glances, [maidens] who have not been touched by any man or jinn before them.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
It is as though they are rubies and pearls.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
And beside these there will be two [other] gardens.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Deep green.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
In both of them will be two gushing fountains.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
In both of them will be fruits and date-palms and pomegranates.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
In them are maidens [who are] good, beautiful
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Houris secluded in pavilions.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Untouched by any man before them or jinn.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Reclining upon green cushions and lovely druggets.
So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
Blessed be the Name of your Lord, He of Majesty and Munificence.
When the [imminent] Event comes to pass,
there will be no denying its coming to pass,
When the earth is shaken with a violent shock,
and the mountains are pulverised to [tiny] pieces,
so that they become a scattered dust,
and you will be three kinds:
Those of the right [hand] — what of those of the right [hand]?
And those of the left [hand] — what of those of the left [hand]?
And the foremost, the foremost:
they are the ones brought near [to God],
in the Gardens of Bliss,
a multitude from the former [generations],
and a few from the later ones
reclining on them, face to face.
They will be waited on by immortal youths
with goblets and ewers and a cup from a flowing spring,
wherefrom they suffer no headache nor any stupefaction,
and such fruits as they prefer,
and such flesh of fowls as they desire,
and houris with wide eyes
resembling hidden pearls,
a reward for what they used to do.
